# Swap — Style Reference

> Unbleached linen lookbook with one keylime sticker on the cover. Hairline serif headlines on a white canvas, sand-toned case cards, 1px stone line work, and a single pale-green button that marks every path to a demo.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Swap speaks an editorial-commerce language: the typography of a fashion lookbook laid over logistics infrastructure. The canvas is pure #ffffff, and tonal steps do the layering instead of lines: #f6f5f3 for secondary buttons and mockup tiles, #eae7e1 for the sand-toned case-study cards, #e3e3e3 for image frames and idle dots, and #2d3636 as the single inverted slate. The chromatic budget is one hue family. Keylime #a3fda7 fills the Book a Demo button, forest #219e73 marks active states, and mint #f2ffe3 washes exactly one section, while everything else stays achromatic. Hierarchy comes from a light serif at weights 100 and 300, stepping 32 → 54 → 80 → 120px at roughly a 1.5 ratio with −0.01em tracking. A neutral grotesk at 400 handles all UI at 15px. Shapes are soft-rounded, with 10px buttons, 20px case cards and 24px panels, and pill inputs are the outlier. Elevation is tonal, with one diffuse shadow rationed to floating mockups. The result reads as a fashion quarterly rather than a SaaS dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Body background, footer, platform feature panels and inverted button text. It is a true white, so the warm neutrals around it read as deliberate tints rather than drift. |
| Linen Button | `#f6f5f3` | `--color-linen-button` | View Video secondary button and dotted mockup tiles inside feature panels (8 uses). It is the quietest warm step, a surface you feel more than see. |
| Sand Card | `#eae7e1` | `--color-sand-card` | Case-study carousel cards, all six of them (10 uses). The warm sand gives editorial photography a paper mount rather than a UI container. |
| Fog Tile | `#e3e3e3` | `--color-fog-tile` | Image frames, hero backdrop panel and inactive pagination dots (14 uses, the most frequent fill). It is a cool neutral reserved for placeholders, so do not use it for text-bearing cards. |
| Carbon Slate | `#2d3636` | `--color-carbon-slate` | Read more buttons, their 1px borders and the dark demo-form panel (10 uses). It is a green-tinted near-black that is the only inverted surface. Do not swap it for pure black. |
| Jet Ink | `#000000` | `--color-jet-ink` | Headlines, nav links, body copy and primary button labels (121 uses). Pure black is the workhorse, and it is softened only by the light serif weights. |
| Onyx Heading | `#080808` | `--color-onyx-heading` | Case-card titles and card body text (30 uses). It is a fractional step off black that keeps sand cards from looking stamped. |
| Pewter Caption | `#777777` | `--color-pewter-caption` | Carousel arrow glyphs, arrow button rings and muted captions (4 uses). It is the only grey text, rationed to controls and asides. |
| Stone Border | `#c7c4be` | `--color-stone-border` | 1px ring around the Retail and Fashion industry tags on sand cards (10 uses). It is a warm hairline tuned to sit on #eae7e1 without contrast spikes. |
| Frosted Hairline | `#ffffff40` | `--color-frosted-hairline` | 1px border of pill inputs on the Carbon Slate form (6 uses). It is a 25%-white line that outlines fields without adding a second dark tone. |
| Keylime Signal | `#a3fda7` | `--color-keylime-signal` | Book a Demo fill and border in the nav and hero (2 fills). It is the entire call-to-action vocabulary. Do not use it for text, icons or large backgrounds. |
| Forest Pulse | `#219e73` | `--color-forest-pulse` | Active carousel dot and the toggle inside the Shipping Zone mockup (2 uses). It is the status shade of the keylime family. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Mint Wash | `#f2ffe3` | `--color-mint-wash` | Top-to-bottom gradient backdrop behind the Agentic Commerce Platform section (1 use). It is an atmospheric tint, not a surface, so keep it off cards and buttons. |

## Tokens — Typography

### secondaryFont — a light, high-contrast display serif that carries every headline and statistic · `--font-secondary-font`

- **Substitute:** Newsreader Display at 300 (use 200 for the 120px numerals), Instrument Serif at 400, Source Serif 4 Display at 300. The original draws heavier than its nominal weight: its 100 renders like a 200 to 250 and its 300 like a 350. Match the hairline-but-legible stroke in the screenshots, not the number, and do not drop to a true Thin.
- **Weights:** 100, 300
- **Sizes:** 32px, 52px, 54px, 60px, 70px, 72px, 80px, 120px
- **Line height:** 0.95, 1.0, 1.02, 1.05
- **Letter spacing:** −0.32px at 32px, −0.52px at 52px, −0.54px at 54px, −0.6px at 60px, −0.7px at 70px, −1.2px at 72px, −0.8px at 80px, −1.2px at 120px (a constant −0.01em, tightened only at 72px)
- **Role:** Weight 300 at 54 to 80px, and 100 at 120px, is the signature. Headlines are enormous and nearly weightless, which is anti-convention for B2B infrastructure, where 600 to 700 sans is the default. The 32 → 54 → 80 → 120px steps run near a 1.5 ratio, steeper than the usual Major Third (1.25), so each level is a distinct event rather than a nudge. Constant −0.01em tracking keeps the serif's ball terminals touching without crowding.

### mainFont — a neutral grotesk that does every UI, body and card-title job · `--font-main-font`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400 (500 for 24px panel titles), Geist at 400, Hanken Grotesk at 400. mainFont draws true to its nominal weight, so no compensation is needed. Avoid Manrope, whose wider set reads bolder at 15px.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 9px, 12px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 22px, 24px, 25px, 30px, 40px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.2, 1.4, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** −0.15px at 15px (weight 300), −0.24px at 24px, −0.625px at 25px, −0.9px at 30px, 0 at 9px, 12px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 22px and 40px
- **Role:** 15px at weight 400 is the workhorse (71 uses), one pixel under the conventional 16px body, which makes nav and buttons read like captions in a magazine. Tracking tightens only from 24px upward (−0.01em to −0.03em), so card titles at 30px pull together while small text stays open. Weight 700 is rationed to 11 inline emphases. The grotesk is the instrument panel to the serif's cover story.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | mainFont | 400 | 9px | 1.2 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | mainFont | 400 | 12px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | mainFont | 400 | 15px | 1.2 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | mainFont | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | mainFont | 400 | 18px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | mainFont | 500 | 24px | 1.2 | −0.24px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | mainFont | 400 | 30px | 1.2 | −0.9px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | secondaryFont | 300 | 54px | 1.05 | −0.54px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | secondaryFont | 300 | 80px | 1.02 | −0.8px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | secondaryFont | 100 | 120px | 0.95 | −1.2px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every section headline in secondaryFont at weight 300 and 54px or 80px with −0.01em tracking — the lightness is the brand, and size alone carries rank.
- Keep #a3fda7 exclusive to the Book a Demo fill — one hue on one action makes the CTA findable on a 100,000px page without decoration.
- Use 10px radius on every clickable rectangle (primary, secondary, inverted) — the shared corner binds three differently colored buttons into one family.
- Layer surfaces tonally: #ffffff, then #f6f5f3, then #eae7e1, then #2d3636 — separation through a 2 to 8% luminance step reads as paper stock, not interface.
- Set UI text at mainFont 15px weight 400 — one pixel below convention gives nav and buttons the scale of magazine captions.
- Mount lifestyle photography edge-to-edge inside 20px sand cards with 0 padding — the image and the card corner are the same object.
- Reserve the md shadow for elements that overlap something (the floating mockup, white panels on #f2ffe3) — shadow means "on top of", not "important".

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis — weight 300 at 80px is the thesis, and a heavy serif turns a fashion quarterly into a law-firm brochure.
- Don't saturate the CTA to a conventional #219e73 fill with white text — the keylime's pastel calm is what lets 300-weight headlines remain the loudest thing on screen.
- Don't add 1px #c7c4be borders around sand cards or white panels — the system separates by tone, and outlines would add a grid the layout deliberately omits.
- Don't round buttons to 100px to match the inputs and tags — pills mean "label" or "field" here, and a pill CTA would erase the click-versus-type distinction.
- Don't replace #2d3636 with #000000 for inverted buttons — the green-tinted slate is the only way the dark element joins the keylime family without spending chroma.
- Don't drop body copy to #777777 for a softer look — Pewter Caption is rationed to 4 control uses, and grey paragraphs would wash out against a 300-weight serif that is already light. This rule is non-negotiable.
- Never spread the #f2ffe3 mint wash across multiple sections — it marks the single product-platform chapter, and repetition turns punctuation into wallpaper.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- secondary surface: #f6f5f3 (Linen Button)
- card surface: #eae7e1 (Sand Card)
- text: #000000 (Jet Ink)
- inverted surface: #2d3636 (Carbon Slate)
- hairline: #c7c4be (Stone Border)
- status: #219e73 (Forest Pulse)
- primary action: #a3fda7 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts stay neutral by default, with series in #2d3636 and #c7c4be on #ffffff. Exactly one highlighted series may use solid #219e73, and #a3fda7 may only appear as a 40%-opacity background band behind that series, so no data mark outshouts the Book a Demo button.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button labeled "Book a Demo": an anchor with display inline-flex, align-items center, height 47px, padding 0 19px, background #a3fda7, border 1px solid #a3fda7, border-radius 10px, color #000000, font-family mainFont (fallback Inter at 400), font-size 15px, font-weight 400, line-height 1.2, letter-spacing 0, and no box-shadow. Place a secondary button beside it with a 12px gap, styled identically except background #f6f5f3, border 1px solid #f6f5f3 and the label "View Video".

2. Build a case-study card: an article 820px wide and 475px tall, background #eae7e1, border-radius 20px, overflow hidden, padding 0, display grid with two equal columns. The left column is a full-bleed object-fit cover photograph. The right column has 32px padding and holds, in a top row, a black brand wordmark at left and an industry tag at right (transparent background, 1px solid #c7c4be border, border-radius 100px, padding 2px 8px, mainFont 12px weight 400, #000000). Below sit a title at mainFont 30px weight 400, line-height 1.2, letter-spacing −0.9px, color #080808; a 15px weight-400 quote in #080808, 12px below; and, pinned to the bottom, a button with background #2d3636, color #ffffff, border-radius 10px, height 47px, padding 0 19px, 15px text "Read more".

3. Build a hero section on #ffffff within a 1200px container and 80px vertical padding, as two columns with a 40px gap. Left column: an h1 in a light serif (Newsreader Display at 300) at 80px, line-height 1.02, letter-spacing −0.8px, color #000000; then an 18px mainFont paragraph at weight 400, line-height 1.4, max-width 450px, 24px below; then the keylime and linen buttons 32px below. Right column: a square photograph on a #e3e3e3 frame with border-radius 10px, overlapped at bottom-left by a white card (background #ffffff, border-radius 10px, padding 24px, box-shadow 0px 14px 32px -20px rgba(0,0,0,0.22), 0px 3px 10px -6px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)) containing a 24px weight-500 title "Shipping Zone" and a toggle filled #219e73.

4. Build a stat row: three equal columns in a 1200px container, no backgrounds or borders. Each holds a numeral in a serif (Newsreader Display at 200) at 120px, line-height 0.95, letter-spacing −1.2px, color #000000, with any "%" as a superscript at 54px, and below it, at a 30px gap, a label in mainFont 18px weight 400, line-height 1.4, color #000000. Use 80px of section padding above and below.

5. Build a navigation bar: height 85px, background #ffffff, no border and no shadow, position relative, inner max-width 1200px with flex space-between. Left: a serif "Swap" wordmark, then links "Services", "Industries", "Resources" (each with a small chevron) and "Customer Stories" in mainFont 15px weight 400, color #000000, padding 4px 6px, gap 24px. Right: a "Sign in" text link styled the same, then the #a3fda7 primary button with 10px radius, 47px height and 0 19px padding, separated by a 24px gap.

## Components

### Primary Button — Keylime (Book a Demo)
**Role:** The single conversion action

Soft-cornered, green, unshouting. The button uses background #a3fda7, text #000000, a 1px solid #a3fda7 border, 10px border-radius, 0 19px padding, a fixed 47px height and mainFont 15px at weight 400 with no shadow. Here the action is announced by hue alone, which keeps it in register with the light serif headlines.

### Secondary Button — Linen (View Video)
**Role:** Low-commitment companion action

A tonal whisper. The button uses background #f6f5f3, text #000000, a 1px border in the same tone, 10px radius, 0 19px padding, 47px height and mainFont 15px at 400 with no shadow. It sits beside the keylime button in the hero and separates from the white canvas by a 2% tonal step rather than an outline, so the pair reads as one unit with a clear first choice.

### Inverted Button — Carbon (Read more)
**Role:** Card-level navigation into stories

The only dark control. The button uses background #2d3636, text #ffffff, a 1px solid #2d3636 border, 10px radius, 0 19px padding, 47px height and mainFont 15px at 400. It lives inside sand cards, where keylime would compete with the photography. The slate's green undertone keeps it in the brand family without spending chroma.

### Circular Arrow Button (Carousel Control)
**Role:** Previous and next for carousels

Outlined, round, grey. The control is 48 × 48px with a transparent background, a 1px solid #777777 border, 50% radius and a #777777 arrow glyph at mainFont 16px. It is the only place Pewter Caption carries an outline. It sits right-aligned on the section heading's baseline row, so navigation reads as a footnote to the headline rather than a toolbar.

### Navigation Bar
**Role:** Top-level wayfinding and demo entry

Flat white band. The bar is 85px tall, background #ffffff, not sticky (position relative), with the serif "Swap" wordmark at left, then Services, Industries and Resources with chevrons plus Customer Stories. Each link is set at mainFont 15px weight 400 in #000000 with 4px 6px padding. Sign in and the #a3fda7 Book a Demo button sit at the right. There is no border and no shadow — the nav refuses chrome so the hero's serif owns the first impression.

### Case-Study Card (Carousel)
**Role:** Customer proof with editorial photography

A magazine spread in a box. Each card is 820 × 475px, background #eae7e1, text #080808, no border, 20px radius and 0 padding. The product photograph bleeds the full left half, and the right half holds the brand wordmark, an industry tag, a 30px mainFont title at 400 with −0.9px tracking, a 15px quote and a Carbon Read more button, inset 32px. The sand mount turns customer logos into lookbook credits.

### Industry Tag Pill
**Role:** Category label on case cards

Hairline lozenge. The tag has a transparent background, a 1px solid #c7c4be border, 100px radius, 2px 8px padding (estimated) and mainFont 12px at 400 in #000000. It sits top-right on sand cards, opposite the brand wordmark. The pill shape breaks from the 10px button corner deliberately, signalling a non-interactive label rather than an action.

### Stat Block
**Role:** Outcome numbers as typography

Numerals as headline. Three columns each hold a secondaryFont figure at 120px, weight 100, line-height 0.95, −1.2px tracking, #000000, with a superscripted % at reduced size and a mainFont 18px weight-400 label 30px below. There is no background, border or icon. Weight 100 at 120px is the system's lightest gesture on its largest element — the proof is stated, not shouted.

### Logo Marquee
**Role:** Social proof row

Monochrome running ticker. A centered secondaryFont heading at 32px weight 300 with −0.32px tracking reads "Powering 1000+ Global Businesses" in #000000. Below it sits a horizontally scrolling row of about eight black customer wordmarks on #ffffff, spaced roughly 60px apart, with no dividers or cards. Keeping the logos black and unboxed lets each brand's own typography do the talking, which suits a fashion-heavy client list.

### Platform Feature Panel
**Role:** Product capability with live mockup

White plate on mint. The panel uses background #ffffff on the #f2ffe3 gradient section, 24px radius, no border, the md shadow and 60px inner padding. Its title is mainFont 24px at 500 with −0.24px tracking in #000000, and the description is 16px at 400. The lower half is an inset #f6f5f3 tile with 10px radius and a decorative dot grid. Two panels sit side by side — this is where the product UI gets shown, framed rather than screenshotted.

### Floating UI Mockup Card
**Role:** Product fragment overlaying photography

Lifted interface shard. The card uses background #ffffff, 10px radius and the md shadow. It overlaps the hero portrait at bottom-left and shows a "Shipping Zone" form with mainFont 15px labels and a #219e73 toggle. It is the only element that floats over imagery, and the shadow exists to sell that overlap — product logic sitting on top of brand lifestyle.

### Pill Input — Dark Form
**Role:** Demo-request field on slate

The system outlier. The field has a transparent background on #2d3636, text #ffffff, a 1px solid #ffffff40 border, 100px radius, 12px 19px 0 padding, 47px height and mainFont 16px at 400. It breaks the 10px control corner deliberately: the pill marks form entry as a different act from clicking, and on the dark panel the frosted hairline reads as glass rather than a box.

### Pagination Dots
**Role:** Carousel position indicator

Rationed status color. Each dot is 6px (estimated) with 50% radius and a gap of 12px (estimated). Inactive dots are #e3e3e3 and the active dot is #219e73. They are centered under the case carousel — one of only two places Forest Pulse appears, so the active state is the single colored pixel in an otherwise neutral section.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every section headline in secondaryFont at weight 300 and 54px or 80px with −0.01em tracking — the lightness is the brand, and size alone carries rank.
- Keep #a3fda7 exclusive to the Book a Demo fill — one hue on one action makes the CTA findable on a 100,000px page without decoration.
- Use 10px radius on every clickable rectangle (primary, secondary, inverted) — the shared corner binds three differently colored buttons into one family.
- Layer surfaces tonally: #ffffff, then #f6f5f3, then #eae7e1, then #2d3636 — separation through a 2 to 8% luminance step reads as paper stock, not interface.
- Set UI text at mainFont 15px weight 400 — one pixel below convention gives nav and buttons the scale of magazine captions.
- Mount lifestyle photography edge-to-edge inside 20px sand cards with 0 padding — the image and the card corner are the same object.
- Reserve the md shadow for elements that overlap something (the floating mockup, white panels on #f2ffe3) — shadow means "on top of", not "important".

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis — weight 300 at 80px is the thesis, and a heavy serif turns a fashion quarterly into a law-firm brochure.
- Don't saturate the CTA to a conventional #219e73 fill with white text — the keylime's pastel calm is what lets 300-weight headlines remain the loudest thing on screen.
- Don't add 1px #c7c4be borders around sand cards or white panels — the system separates by tone, and outlines would add a grid the layout deliberately omits.
- Don't round buttons to 100px to match the inputs and tags — pills mean "label" or "field" here, and a pill CTA would erase the click-versus-type distinction.
- Don't replace #2d3636 with #000000 for inverted buttons — the green-tinted slate is the only way the dark element joins the keylime family without spending chroma.
- Don't drop body copy to #777777 for a softer look — Pewter Caption is rationed to 4 control uses, and grey paragraphs would wash out against a 300-weight serif that is already light. This rule is non-negotiable.
- Never spread the #f2ffe3 mint wash across multiple sections — it marks the single product-platform chapter, and repetition turns punctuation into wallpaper.

| 0 | Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | Page body, nav, footer, logo marquee and platform panels |

## Elevation

- **Floating UI mockup over hero photography and white platform panels on the mint wash:** `0px 14px 32px -20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.22), 0px 3px 10px -6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`

That is the entire shadow vocabulary — 4 uses on the page. The −20px spread pulls the 32px blur in under the element, so the shadow pools beneath like a sheet resting on a table rather than haloing outward. Everything else, including buttons, nav, case cards and the stat row, is flat, and separation comes from the tonal stack above.

## Imagery

Imagery is fashion and lifestyle photography, the dominant visual material: a portrait with jewelry in the hero, a sneaker, a crocodile clutch on saturated red, and a model in black on grey. Each image is mounted full-bleed into the left half of a 20px #eae7e1 case card, or sits square in a #e3e3e3 frame at 10px radius, with no borders and no shadows on photographs. Product UI appears as reconstructed mockups, never raw screenshots: white 10px cards with the md shadow, form fields, toggles in #219e73, and flowchart nodes in black pills on #f6f5f3 dot-grid tiles. Icons are thin, monoline and functional (chevrons, arrows, a rocket glyph), and the photographs' red backdrops are decorative, not system tokens. The single gradient is the #f2ffe3 mint wash, used once. The narrative is clear: brands bring the beauty, Swap supplies the quiet machinery underneath.

## Layout

Content holds a 1200px max-width inside a 1960px outer frame, with sections separated by 80px (70px for tighter transitions). The hero is a two-column split: on the left, a small badge, an 80px weight-300 serif headline with a rotating last word, an 18px paragraph and the keylime and linen buttons; on the right, a large photograph overlaid by the floating mockup card. Sections then alternate between white and tinted grounds: logo marquee, case-card carousel with arrows right-aligned to a 54px heading, a three-column stat row, then the mint-washed platform chapter introduced by an uppercase 15px eyebrow above a two-column grid of feature panels. The nav is 85px, white and non-sticky, with the logo and four links at left and Sign in plus Book a Demo at right. The footer is a white, multi-column link field roughly 1154px tall. At 375px, set the h1 at 54px and stat numerals at 80px, collapse all grids to one column and use a 40px section gap. Overall density is spacious.

## Hairline Serif Discipline

The system's defining move is a weight 100 and 300 serif at 54 to 120px on a commerce-infrastructure site, where convention calls for 600 to 700 sans. Everything else is tuned to protect that lightness. Body is plain 400 grotesk, text is pure #000000 for maximum contrast against thin strokes, and nothing competes for weight. The discipline breaks the moment anyone bolds a headline for emphasis, sets the serif below 32px (where hairlines vanish), or swaps in a substitute whose 300 renders as a true Light. Extend it by adding sizes on the 1.5 ratio only. A new section heading goes at 54px weight 300, not at a new 42px weight 500. Emphasis inside a headline comes from a rotating word or a second line, never from weight.

## Keylime Rationing

The chromatic budget is one hue family and three values: #a3fda7 for the action, #219e73 for active state, #f2ffe3 for one atmospheric wash. The whole 100,000px page contains two keylime fills, which is why the Book a Demo button is findable without arrows or animation. The system breaks if keylime becomes a link color, an icon tint, a badge or a section background, or if a second hue such as an error red or info blue enters chrome. Extend it by deriving new states from the existing set. Success uses #219e73, selection uses a #f6f5f3 fill with a #000000 label, and any warning lives in copy, not color. Photography may carry any hue it likes, because it is content rather than chrome.

## Tonal Stacking

Swap separates elements by paper stock, not by lines or lift. The stack runs #ffffff → #f6f5f3 → #eae7e1 → #2d3636, each step a distinct material: page, sleeve, mount, cover. Borders appear only where tone cannot work: 1px #c7c4be on tags that sit on sand, 1px #777777 on arrow rings over white, and 1px #ffffff40 on fields over slate. The system breaks if cards gain outlines, if shadows spread beyond the 4 overlap cases, or if a fifth grey such as a cool #f5f7fa slips in, because it would fight the warm undertone of #f6f5f3 and #eae7e1. Extend it by picking new surfaces from the existing four only. Any new container chooses a level, not a new color.

## Similar Brands

- **Aesop** — Shares the warm sand-and-linen neutral stack and light editorial serif headlines, but Aesop has no saturated CTA, while Swap spends exactly one keylime fill.
- **Mercury** — Shares light-weight display type on a fintech-grade product and tonal rather than bordered surfaces, though Mercury's surfaces run cool where Swap's run warm.
- **Loop Returns** — A direct category competitor in post-purchase and returns, sharing case-study carousels built on brand photography, but Loop uses heavy sans headlines and multiple saturated hues where Swap holds to a 300 serif and one green.
- **Global-e** — A cross-border commerce competitor with the same "go global" positioning, yet its corporate blue system and bold sans read as enterprise software, the opposite of Swap's lookbook register.
- **SSENSE** — Shares the fashion-editorial grammar of black wordmarks on white, full-bleed product photography and near-zero chrome, which is the visual world Swap's customers come from.
